observation.visible_scene: A black-and-white vehicle labeled "HUMDINGA" (with "CHEER AMPHIBIANS" near the cockpit) runs along a paved test track. It has a boat-like pointed bow, an open top cockpit, two visible axles/wheels, and a seated driver whose head and arm are visible. The clip is shot from the side with a tracking camera that holds the vehicle roughly centered while the tree-lined background and the grass foreground appear horizontally motion-blurred, indicating the vehicle is in motion. Red-and-white trackside cones/barrels become visible along the edge of the track in the later part of the sequence. The final frame is a different, wider view of a curving stretch of the track (sky and distant trees visible) with the same vehicle blurred at the right edge.
visible_changes: The vehicle travels steadily along the track; relative to the frame it drifts slightly leftward then rightward as the camera tracks it, but stays approximately centered throughout the tracking portion.
A side-pan/tracking camera produces continuous horizontal motion blur in the background and foreground.
Red-and-white cones/barrels appear at the trackside from roughly the middle-to-late frames onward.
An editing cut at the last frame switches to a wide, different-angle shot of a curved track section, with the vehicle now at the right edge and heavily blurred.
The vehicle's livery, open cockpit, bow orientation (pointed end to the right), and the presence of one driver remain constant across the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: The vehicle's actual speed and whether it is moving left or right in world coordinates (the tracking camera keeps it centered).
What happens before the first frame and after the last frame, including any transition to water or stop.
The purpose of the track and the red/white markers.
Whether the wide final view is a separate shot of the same run or a different moment.
uncertain_details: The small horizontal drift of the vehicle within the frame could be camera tracking lag or genuine relative motion; not determinable.
The exact nature of the trackside objects (cones vs. barrels) is blurred.
The vehicle's direction of travel relative to the world is inferred from its bow orientation, not directly measured.
The relationship between the tracking shots and the final wide shot is a cut, not continuous physical motion.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
